_comment: Hero Designer's Modifier.included() verdict for every question the modifier-checking code asks of tests/validation_sink.py, loaded as a real character (not a template prototype -- this measures the LOADER too). Regenerate with kirby-hd-oracle: venv/bin/python -c "from tests.validation_sink import write; print(write('/tmp/ValidationSink.hdc'))" then (cd ../kirby-hd-oracle && ./hd6cli.sh --included /tmp/ValidationSink.hdc) > tests/fixtures/included_stateful.json -- required whenever Main6E.hdt, the oracle, or the sink changes. Three tiers, one row shape (spec section 3): `template` (every template modifier x this loaded object -- HD's Modifier.getIncluded() prototype check, same question as the prototype matrix but against a REAL loaded object's state instead of a bare template prototype); `assigned` (each modifier already attached to the object, re-asked -- verifyModifiers()'s plain-object loop, GenericObject.java); `framework` (each framework-common modifier x each slot in a Multipower/VPP -- verifyModifiers()'s List walk, which adds every OTHER missing common modifier to the slot before asking, matching the engine harness's own with_siblings construction; Elemental Control never produces a framework-tier row and, since Task 3 fix round 1, the sink no longer authors one at all -- Main6E.hdt (this character's template) has no ELEMENTALCONTROL entry; 6E replaced the framework with the plain UNIFIEDPOWER Limitation, which the sink now carries on two plain powers instead). A `via_compound` field on a framework row names the Compound Power the constituent (`object_id`) sits inside; `parent_id` is always the enclosing List, never the compound. `state` is HD's own echo of the object's duration, END usage, active cost, range, defense, damage/body/knockback flags and target at ask time -- what the verdict was actually computed from, not part of the key. The Characteristic-clone simplification from Task 1: RUNNING/SWIMMING/LEAPING rows ask against the loaded Characteristic clone the same way the prototype matrix's template_power() does, not a synthesized power.
